survivors.title: Runtime discovery walks to the nearest .memory-seed
survivors.decision: Runtime discovery uses nearest-ancestor `.memory-seed/` directory, walking upward from current working directory to find the active runtime.
survivors.why: Canonical runtime location enables portable memory systems and supports nested sub-project runtimes with automatic scoping.
survivors.evolution: Founded from the control file; no session lineage attached yet.
survivors.source_quote: Runtime discovery walks upward from `cwd` and uses the nearest `.memory-seed/`.

_assigned.title: Runtime discovery walks to the nearest .memory-seed

survivors.title: Four never-merged edge kinds, forward-only and acyclic
survivors.decision: Lifecycle edges comprise four never-merged kinds: `replaces`, `evolves`, `related_entries`, and `evolved_by` (inverse). Edges are forward-only and acyclic by contract.
survivors.why: Four independent relationship claims deserve distinct semantic labels. Forward-only and acyclic structure ensures the edge graph is append-only and prevents cycles in artifact lineage.
survivors.evolution: Founded from the control file; no session lineage attached yet.
survivors.source_quote: Evolution edges and artifact lineage (core shipped in 2.18.0; Trace continuity completed 2026-07-15): typed `evolves:` plus read-time `evolved_by`, inverse-field and continuity validation

_assigned.title: Four never-merged edge kinds, forward-only and acyclic

survivors.title: Scored topic auto-backfill rejected; curated-evidence premise adopted
survivors.decision: Automated topic backfill with scoring gates is rejected. Manual, curated attribution is adopted: one worker per batch judges all decision units and writes final topic assignments without automated scoring.
survivors.why: Two pilot runs scored macro-recall at 58.3% and 61.3% against a 0.70 gate, falling short. The curated-evidence premise succeeded: a human worker with swarm output as evidence judged 1,030 units and wrote 2,013 attributions (95% carrying both axes).
survivors.evolution: Founded from the control file; no session lineage attached yet.
survivors.source_quote: Decision-level topic judgment swarm — **the scored auto-backfill was piloted twice and explicitly ABORTED (2026-07-26)**: two pilot runs scored macro-recall 0.583 and 0.613 against a 0.70 gate
survivors.binding_note: Status: rejected. Scored automation was empirically measured and fell short of the gate; curated-evidence pathway succeeded instead.

_assigned.title: Scored topic auto-backfill rejected; curated-evidence premise adopted

survivors.title: Month-grouped session layout; per-user gated on 2+ participants
survivors.decision: Session document discovery uses iter_session_documents() to read legacy flat session files (sessions/YYYY-MM-DD.md), new month-grouped flat files (sessions/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md), and new month-grouped per-user files (sessions/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD/<user>.md). Per-user layout activates only when 2+ participants are registered.
survivors.why: Month grouping organizes session history by calendar period for better discoverability; per-user gating prevents fragmentation for single-user projects while supporting team workflows when participants are declared.
survivors.evolution: Founded from the control file; no session lineage attached yet.
survivors.source_quote: Session document discovery: package readers use `iter_session_documents()` in `core.py` to read legacy flat session files (`sessions/YYYY-MM-DD.md`), legacy per-day/per-user files (`sessions/YYYY-MM-DD/<user>.md`), new month-grouped flat files (`sessions/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`), and new month-grouped per-user files (`sessions/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD/<user>.md`).

supporting.quote: The migration parses each legacy `sessions/YYYY-MM-DD.md` entry, maps entry `user_initials` through `.memory-seed/project.yaml` `participants:`, writes/appends to `sessions/YYYY-MM-DD/<user>.md`

_assigned.title: Month-grouped session layout; per-user gated on 2+ participants

survivors.title: Deterministic 80-bit mse_ ids; legacy ms- never rewritten
survivors.decision: New generated session entry_id values use deterministic 80-bit mse_ IDs encoded in 16 lower-case Base32 characters. Legacy ms- IDs remain valid forever and are never rewritten.
survivors.why: 80 bits is the practical middle ground for collision risk at team scale, materially shorter than 128-bit visible IDs, and negligible collision risk for plausible Memory Seed corpora. Preserving legacy IDs maintains append-only immutability and backward compatibility.
survivors.evolution: Evolved in mse_77cn2v0rg9na3w0v:d1 where generate_session_entry_id() was implemented to emit deterministic mse_ IDs using SHA-256 and Crockford/Base32 alphabet.
survivors.source_quote: Entry-ID widening + MCP metadata filters (shipped 2.12.0): new generated session `entry_id` values use deterministic 80-bit `mse_` IDs while legacy `ms-` IDs remain valid and are never rewritten.

_assigned.title: Deterministic 80-bit mse_ ids; legacy ms- never rewritten

survivors.title: DRAFT single-decision baseline; D/R mandatory; numbered decisions canonical
survivors.decision: The single-decision DRAFT record is the baseline session-entry shape. D/R (Decision/Rationale) are mandatory fields; A/F/T (Alternatives/Findings/Tests) are optional. Multi-decision entries use numbered #### Dn headings as the canonical form.
survivors.why: A baseline structure with mandatory decision rationale ensures every memory entry captures the core reasoning. Explicit numbering makes multi-decision entries unambiguous and discoverable.
survivors.evolution: Founded from the control file; established as baseline in 2.4.0 per the control plane history.
survivors.source_quote: The single-decision DRAFT record is the **baseline** session-entry shape (since 2.4.0); the bare summary (simpler) and multi-decision (richer) shapes are explicit routes off it. D/R are mandatory, A/F/T optional.

_assigned.title: DRAFT single-decision baseline; D/R mandatory; numbered decisions canonical

survivors.title: Branch-session fuse: branch-only, chronological, immutable relative to base
survivors.decision: memory-seed session fuse --branch <branch> dry-runs and applies branch-local session entries and diagram sidecars. Imported entries must be branch-only, chronological, immutable relative to base, and carry `branch: <branch>` metadata.
survivors.why: Chronological immutability relative to the base preserves append-only ordering when merging branch work. The branch metadata enables recovery and validation during structured fuse.
survivors.evolution: Founded from the control file; implements the structural session merge capability.
survivors.source_quote: Branch-session fuse (current unreleased worktree): `memory-seed session fuse --branch <branch>` dry-runs branch-local session entries and diagram sidecars before promotion, and `--apply` writes only during an in-progress `git merge --no-ff --no-commit <branch>`. Imported entries must be branch-only, chronological, immutable relative to base, and carry `branch: <branch>`.

_assigned.title: Branch-session fuse: branch-only, chronological, immutable relative to base

survivors.title: Configurable integration_mode: local-merge vs PR
survivors.decision: integration_mode is a project-local default read fail-open as local-merge, surfaced by ESR, obeyed by live+seed agent contracts, and implemented by mode-aware session integrate plus session open-pr.
survivors.why: Different workflows require different integration strategies: local-merge for single-developer rapid iteration, PR for team review gates. Configurable mode lets projects choose without code changes.
survivors.evolution: Founded from the control file; completed 2026-07-15 per the control plane history.
survivors.source_quote: Configurable integration mode (completed 2026-07-15): `integration_mode: local-merge|pr` is a project-local default read fail-open as `local-merge`, surfaced by ESR, obeyed by live+seed agent contracts, and implemented by mode-aware `session integrate` plus `session open-pr`.

_assigned.title: Configurable integration_mode: local-merge vs PR

survivors.title: Agent-config JSON/TOML merge, never seed-copy
survivors.decision: Handle agent config files as JSON/TOML merge targets during init/update, preserving existing project configuration rather than overwriting.
survivors.why: Most projects already have .claude/settings.json with permissions, model, and other settings. Using seed-file copy would fail on existing projects or silently wipe their configuration.
survivors.evolution: Founded May 2026 (ms-56fdf2ad); merge pattern established in core.py _merge_claude_hook and _merge_codex_hook functions.
survivors.source_quote: `.claude/settings.json` and `.codex/hooks.json` are handled as JSON merge targets during init/update — not seed file copies — so existing agent config is preserved.

_assigned.title: Agent-config JSON/TOML merge, never seed-copy

survivors.title: Archive control-plane snapshots before replacing versioned artifacts
survivors.decision: Archive prior control-plane snapshots under .memory-seed/archive/<version>/ before replacing reusable versioned artifacts.
survivors.why: Preserves audit trail of control-plane evolution and enables recovery if a replacement is found to be incorrect or incomplete.
survivors.evolution: Founded from the control file; no session lineage attached yet.
survivors.source_quote: Archive prior control-plane snapshots under `.memory-seed/archive/<version>/` before replacing reusable versioned artifacts.

_assigned.title: Archive control-plane snapshots before replacing versioned artifacts

survivors.title: Publish via GitHub Release with manual PyPI gate
survivors.decision: Publishing is triggered by GitHub Release creation, which activates the publish.yml workflow. The pypi environment has a manual-approval gate that a reviewer must approve before the PyPI push executes.
survivors.why: GitHub Release creation produces labeled versions in the Actions UI. Manual approval gate ensures human review before the irreversible PyPI deployment and catches any unintended releases.
survivors.evolution: Founded May 2026 (ms-1e38c75c); established as core release policy with multiple releases following the pattern.
survivors.source_quote: Publishing should be triggered by GitHub Release creation, not direct workflow dispatch.

_assigned.title: Publish via GitHub Release with manual PyPI gate

survivors.title: Trace startup incremental; immutable git derivations persist
survivors.decision: Memory Trace startup is incremental: immutable git derivations (fork points, commit parents, changed paths) persist across rebuilds, reconciliation is incremental, and file-entry index is lazy.
survivors.why: Incremental startup drastically improves performance. Warm start reduced from 44.25s to ~308ms; persisted derivations and lazy indexing enable efficient rebuilds and reconciliation.
survivors.evolution: Implemented 2026-07-21 (mse_42e8zzd7); completed the derived-projection plan's final deferred piece.
survivors.source_quote: Memory Trace startup is incremental as of 2026-07-21: immutable git derivations (fork points, commit parents, changed paths) persist across rebuilds, reconciliation is incremental, and the file-entry index is lazy.

_assigned.title: Trace startup incremental; immutable git derivations persist

survivors.title: Trail derives display lanes without authored graph edges
survivors.decision: Trail generates continuity lanes derived from lifecycle edges without requiring or adding authored graph edges.
survivors.why: Reduces manual edge annotation burden; derived lanes stay synchronized with true causality and evolution chain topology without user needing to draw additional edges.
survivors.evolution: Shipped in Wave 1 (2026-07-15) as part of Trace continuity features; plan documented in docs/5_Completed/evolution-edges-plan.md.
survivors.source_quote: Trail derives display lanes without adding authored graph edges.

_assigned.title: Trail derives display lanes without authored graph edges

survivors.title: Topology-community detection measured and rejected
survivors.decision: Reject topology-community detection for graph layout based on corpus-density measurement. The feature does not gate B0b acceptance.
survivors.why: Measured corpus density and found community detection does not improve layout effectiveness for this corpus. Alternative force-based layout achieves the required visualization quality.
survivors.evolution: Measured and rejected 2026-07-26 (mse_fud39yw86e7v2uy); decision recorded to document evaluation rather than defer the feature.
survivors.source_quote: Topology-community detection was measured and closed 2026-07-26 (rejected, not deferred)

_assigned.title: Topology-community detection measured and rejected

survivors.title: Encoding policy owned by Seed, never duplicated in Trace
survivors.decision: Encoding policy (UTF-8, LF, NFC normalization) is owned and enforced by Memory Seed core, never duplicated in Memory Trace.
survivors.why: Memory Trace depends on the core package. One owner keeps UTF-8/LF/NFC policy, exclusions, and backup behavior consistent across the system.
survivors.evolution: Established 2026-07-08 (mse_ejpbz4qqsbdx0hvc); encoding hardening P0 completed with explicit check/repair tooling in Seed.
survivors.source_quote: Encoding policy stays owned by Memory Seed rather than being duplicated in Memory Trace, and `doctor` provides a non-fatal summary.

_assigned.title: Encoding policy owned by Seed, never duplicated in Trace

survivors.title: Docs taxonomy: folder is lifecycle state
survivors.decision: Document lifecycle state is encoded in folder structure. Incoming material enters `docs/1_Inbox/`, active roadmap items sit in `docs/2_Todo/`, live normative specs occupy `docs/3_Spec/` (with candidates in `draft/`), source research lives in `docs/4_Reference/`, and terminal outcomes occupy `docs/5_Completed/`, `6_Rejected/`, `7_Replaced/`, or `8_Deferred/`.
survivors.why: Folder structure makes lifecycle state transparent and queryable. The legacy archive `docs/2_Todo/completed/` was retired 2026-07-17, moving its 43 documents and nested structures to `docs/5_Completed/`, ensuring every terminal document sits in a designated lane.
survivors.evolution: Control-plane decision recorded and codified in the runtime index. Session decision mse_m0xs623m4cs0kjag:d1 (2026-07-15) captured the seeded docs lifecycle as an unapproved proposal, noting that richer lifecycle behavior requires local proof and non-destructive adoption semantics before becoming reusable seed behavior.
survivors.source_quote: Docs taxonomy: `docs/1_Inbox/` holds unassessed incoming material; `docs/2_Todo/` holds active roadmap proposals; `docs/3_Spec/` holds live normative specs (with candidates in `draft/`); `docs/4_Reference/` holds source research; and terminal outcomes live in `docs/5_Completed/`, `6_Rejected/`, `7_Replaced/`, or `8_Deferred/`.

_assigned.title: Docs taxonomy: folder is lifecycle state

survivors.title: business/ separate from docs/; documents move, never copy
survivors.decision: Commercial strategy material lives in `business/` as authoritative dossiers and supporting provenance reports, deliberately separated from `docs/` which holds product specification and implementation lifecycle. Documents move from `docs/4_Reference/` into `business/` rather than being copied; a document has one canonical home.
survivors.why: This separation preserves single-source authority for business strategy while keeping `docs/` focused on product and implementation. Moving documents (not copying) ensures consistency and eliminates duplication.
survivors.evolution: Founded from the control file. Session decision mse_5y962348e85x7grr (2026-08-03) registered `business/` in the runtime index's Topology section after the area was created but initially undocumented, correcting a gap in agent orientation.
survivors.source_quote: **Business knowledge area: `business/`** — commercial strategy, kept deliberately separate from `docs/`, which holds product specification and implementation lifecycle.

supporting.quote: Add `business/` to the runtime index's Topology section

_assigned.title: business/ separate from docs/; documents move, never copy

survivors.title: Experiment fixture isolation is structural via nearest-runtime discovery
survivors.decision: Experimental fixtures achieve isolation through structural design via nearest-runtime discovery. Each generated fixture is a standalone git repository with its own `.memory-seed/` runtime. Fixture runtimes are throwaway sub-project runtimes deliberately not individually registered in the parent index.
survivors.why: Isolation is structural and was proven at build time: a fixture write left the parent corpus counts unchanged. Nearest-runtime discovery provides automatic, predictable fixture isolation without requiring manual registration or explicit isolation machinery.
survivors.evolution: Founded from the control file; outlined in the agent-capture experiment specification. Session decision mse_vaz9d3h7x4bcmd1t:d1 (2026-08-04) narrowed isolation assertion to the parent session store specifically, refining the validation claim while preserving structural isolation.
survivors.source_quote: Isolation is structural (nearest-runtime discovery) and was proven at build time: a fixture write left the parent corpus counts unchanged.

_assigned.title: Experiment fixture isolation is structural via nearest-runtime discovery

survivors.title: Plain-Markdown core for file-reading agents
survivors.decision: The memory core is kept as plain Markdown and predictable for file-reading agents. All critical control-plane files, session logs, and decision records are encoded in readable, human-editable Markdown rather than binary or structured formats.
survivors.why: Plain Markdown preserves local ownership, direct human editing, attribution, and immutable source entries while remaining accessible to file-reading agents without special parsing libraries. This enables append-only discipline and supports both human review and automated agent access.
survivors.evolution: Control-plane behavioral constraint. Session decision mse_ddba1ztxqhasfbwf:d1 (2026-07-16) ratified partitioned Markdown authority with an append-only ADR sidecar, formalizing that original entries and decision updates own rationale/evidence while derived artifacts (registries, indexes, databases) remain secondary.
survivors.source_quote: Keep the memory core plain Markdown and predictable for file-reading agents.

_assigned.title: Plain-Markdown core for file-reading agents

survivors.title: Legacy .AGENTS/ compatibility retained until intentional removal
survivors.decision: Legacy `.AGENTS/` projects continue to be supported in code. Compatibility is preserved unless intentionally removed through an explicit deprecation process, ensuring that existing projects remain functional across version updates.
survivors.why: Removing legacy support silently breaks existing projects. Backward compatibility ensures smooth adoption and gives projects clear signal when a legacy feature is being retired. Ours-only deletion logic (only removing entries we authored, not foreign customizations) protects user investments.
survivors.evolution: Founded from the control file; control-plane policy ratified 2.3.0+. Session decision ms-6a09aea8:d2 (2026-06-03) implemented the specific legacy compatibility mechanism: stripping the obsolete `mcpServers` block from `.claude/settings.json` only when Memory Seed authored the entry.
survivors.source_quote: Preserve compatibility for legacy `.AGENTS/` projects in code unless intentionally removing a legacy path.

_assigned.title: Legacy .AGENTS/ compatibility retained until intentional removal

survivors.title: Worktree=session, branch=task, agent-namespaced branch names
survivors.decision: Worktree hygiene follows a strict naming and lifecycle convention: one worktree per session, one branch per task or feature. New branches follow the pattern `<agent>/<kind>/<topic>` to encode agent identity, work kind (fix, feature, docs, etc.), and topic area.
survivors.why: This convention ensures clear traceability between Git artifacts, session scope, and agent work. Agent-namespaced branches prevent collisions in shared environments and make it easy to identify which agent or session created which branch. Single worktree per session simplifies cleanup and lifecycle management.
survivors.evolution: Founded from the control file; no session lineage attached yet.
survivors.source_quote: The worktree hygiene plan uses worktree=session, branch=task, and `<agent>/<kind>/<topic>` for new branches.

_assigned.title: Worktree=session, branch=task, agent-namespaced branch names

survivors.title: Controlled topic vocabulary with axis hierarchy and seed/live parity
survivors.decision: `topics:` is a first-class entry field resolved against the project-local `.memory-seed/topics.yaml` registry, which implements a two-axis hierarchical vocabulary. The starter vocabulary shipped with Memory Seed is domain-neutral and flat, carrying two axes: areas and activities. Authored topics rank in a declared precedence order with sidecar and inferred topics.
survivors.why: A controlled vocabulary ensures consistent topic use across the corpus and enables coherent navigation and filtering. Two axes (area and activity) remain orthogonal and domain-neutral, supporting software projects, legal matters, research, and other domains. Flat starter vocabulary respects the principle that depth is earned through concentration.
survivors.evolution: Implemented 2026-07-15; redesigned into two-axis hierarchy 2026-07-26/27. Session decision mse_zhf4a0fsgwh47c9j:d1 (2026-07-26) shipped the neutral starter vocabulary, replacing a software-centric starter that had no area axis at all.
survivors.source_quote: Indexed topics (completed 2026-07-15; **redesigned into a two-axis hierarchy 2026-07-26/27**): `topics:` is a first-class entry field resolved against the deploy-once project-local `.memory-seed/topics.yaml`

_assigned.title: Controlled topic vocabulary with axis hierarchy and seed/live parity
